clue.text: Ridiculous pseuds holding potty assumptions are like this

indicators.note: holding means the jumbled pseuds keeps the next piece within it
something ridiculous is absurdly out of order, so the letters of pseuds are jumbled

parts.note: a potty is a child's chamber pot, a PO in crossword shorthand

explanation.surface: A sneer at pretentious people and their silly presumptions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' reads as an adjective meaning daft, but it is the noun: a child's pot. 'Ridiculous' gives the jumble SUPSED, which 'holding' splits around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Assumptions are things taken for granted, so they are, by nature, merely presumed rather than proved.

clue.text: Suffering so, a comic hits out, liking to dish it out as well as take it?

definitions.text: liking to dish it out as well as take it?

parts.note: sad means unhappy or suffering

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A comedian lashes out in distress, both giving and receiving punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hits out' looks like lashing out; only 'out' is the jumbling signal, making OMASOCHISTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: This describes enjoying both inflicting and receiving pain, the combination of sadist and masochist.

clue.text: Tyre burned by local teens?

parts.note: one's local is one's neighbourhood pub

indicators.note: burned suggests something wrecked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Teenagers setting fire to a tyre next to the village pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burned' gives the jumble ERTY; 'by' merely places it beside the local.
explanation.definitionFit: The teenage years are when adolescents develop sexually, roughly matching that stage of growth.

clue.text: Not batting well? Don't rely on your team for help!

definitions.text: Don't rely on your team for help!

parts.note: in cricket a batsman who is out is no longer batting
a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: A cricketer out of form is told not to count on teammates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' seems to be an adverb but is a spring, a source.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract work to an outside supplier is to stop depending on your own staff.

clue.text: Tests cut up manuscript

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the letters are written bottom to top

parts.note: to axe is to cut

explanation.surface: Examinations reduce a written manuscript to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AXE into EXA.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal school and university tests are commonly called by this short plural.

clue.text: Middle Eastern agents surrounding pub backing west

indicators.note: in an across entry, backing west means reading right to left
surrounding means the agents' letters go around the pub

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency, a body of agents
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: Spies from the region staking out a pub on the western side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' splits the agents as CI and A around the pub, making CIBARA, which 'backing west' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabic is the language and culture of much of the Middle East, so it serves as an adjective for the region.

clue.text: Visit Arsenal, perhaps, to back French gentleman

parts.note: to rear is to back or bring up
M is the abbreviation for monsieur

explanation.surface: A Frenchman going to watch Arsenal FC to support the team.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal looks like the London football club, but is an armoury: going to one again is to get weapons once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking weapons from an arsenal again means re-equipping with arms.

clue.text: Take care of section wherein lies bottomless, bottomless pit

indicators.note: wherein lies means the next piece sits inside the section

parts.note: a bit is a section or piece

indicators.note: bottomless means the final letter is removed

parts.note: an abyss is a bottomless pit

explanation.surface: An odd instruction to look after part of a bottomless chasm.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word is the trick: one 'bottomless' belongs to the pit's own name, the other trims its last letter. 'wherein lies' then places the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To mind a child while its parents are away is to look after it.

clue.text: Avoiding batting, perhaps, and not wanting to be pressed

definitions.meaning: a batter stands at the crease, so one resisting the crease is shunning batting
fabric treated so it does not wrinkle needs no ironing

explanation.surface: A reluctant cricketer who also hates being pushed.
explanation.walkthrough: The crease is the marked line where a cricket batter stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric labelled this way keeps its shape and needs no ironing; the cricket reading is a jokey second sense.

clue.text: Promote advertisement about taking part in election

indicators.note: taking part in means the about letters are placed within the election word

parts.note: a vote is an election
CA, circa, means about

explanation.surface: A campaign advert being used during an election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking part in' is the containment signal: circa sits within the ballot word.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak up in favour of a cause or policy is to champion and recommend it.

clue.text: Society girl of one kind and another finding character with means to pay

parts.note: a deb, or debutante, is a young woman entering high society
an It girl is another kind of society girl, so It is the other half of the pair
a card is an amusing character or wag

explanation.surface: A socialite discovering an eccentric with plenty of money.
explanation.walkthrough: The two kinds of society girl are the debutante and the It girl, giving DEB then IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank card that draws straight from your account is a common way of settling a bill.

clue.text: Do in th' blasted Lambeth Walk!

indicators.note: to do in is to destroy, so these letters are knocked out of the street name
blasted means blown apart, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: th' is the shortened 'the', giving the two letters to remove

explanation.surface: A cheery cry to perform the famous Cockney dance song, the Lambeth Walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do in th'' removes TH from LAMBETH, and 'blasted' rearranges what remains, LAMBE. The Lambeth Walk is a 1930s London dance from the musical Me and My Girl.
explanation.definitionFit: To stroll unhurriedly is a gentle way of walking, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Main road mistakes — start off without using these!

definitions.text: Main road mistakes — start off without using these!

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written here with I for the one

indicators.note: start off means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: errors are mistakes

explanation.surface: Driving advice: on the motorway, never pull away without checking behind you.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the London-to-Leeds motorway; its 1 reads as I. The whole clue is also the definition: drivers are taught never to pull out without checking them.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving instructors insist on a glance in the rear-view and wing glasses before moving off, as missing that check causes accidents.

clue.text: Carbon-free world is slowly filtering through

indicators.note: carbon-free means the world is without its C

parts.note: the cosmos is the whole world or universe
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: An environmental slogan: a decarbonised planet is gradually seeping through.
explanation.walkthrough: COSMOS minus C leaves OSMOS, then IS is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmosis is the gradual passage of a solvent through a membrane, and figuratively any slow absorption.

clue.text: Casting one less keen on performing?

definitions.meaning: one who shies, that is throws or casts, at a target, as at a coconut shy
more timid, so less eager to get up on stage

explanation.surface: A theatre audition note about a reluctant actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casting' suggests a director's casting, but it is throwing: a shy is a throw.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a thrower; the other is the comparative of timid, so more reluctant to perform.

clue.text: He's responsible for kids getting grades in gym and religion overturned

indicators.note: in means the grades are placed inside the gym letters

parts.note: PT, physical training, is school gym
ranks are grades or levels

indicators.note: overturned means the religion letters are flipped round

parts.note: RE is religious education, the school subject

explanation.surface: A teacher in charge of grading pupils in PE and RE classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kids' looks like children but is the verb: to kid is to tease. 'overturned' turns RE into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who kids, teasing and playing tricks, is a joker who plays practical jokes.

clue.text: After pub, I drunkenly confess online fraud

parts.note: PH, public house, is the abbreviation for a pub

indicators.note: drunkenly suggests slurred speech, where an s comes out as sh

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing to the police

explanation.surface: After the pub, a drunk admits to a cybercrime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunkenly' slurs SING to SHING.
explanation.definitionFit: This is sending fake emails to trick people into giving away passwords or bank details over the internet.

clue.text: Reject drink

definitions.meaning: a rejection or rebuff, as a noun
to drink quickly, gulping a drink down

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a rebuff and a gulp, as in downing a pint.

clue.text: Brand attracted that woman's attention, 'e said

indicators.note: 'e said, with its dropped h, signals a Cockney pronouncing the phrase

parts.note: attracted her attention is caught her eyes, with the h dropped in Cockney fashion

explanation.surface: A Cockney man explains how a fashion label caught a woman's eye.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the H, a Cockney says 'caught 'er eyes', which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To brand is to burn a mark into flesh with hot iron, which is to sear tissue in a medical sense.

clue.text: Suffer in one language and therefore in another

parts.note: und is German for and
ergo is Latin for therefore

explanation.surface: Pain expressed in one tongue and then, consequently, another.
explanation.walkthrough: The two languages are German and Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: To experience or endure something unpleasant, such as an operation, is to go through it.

clue.text: Watering hole's old and unchanged

parts.note: as is means left unchanged

explanation.surface: A favourite pub has been left exactly as it always was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watering hole' suggests a pub, but here it is a desert spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile desert spot with a well is literally where travellers and animals go to drink.

clue.text: Substitute shoots skyward before interval

indicators.note: skyward, in a down entry, means read from bottom to top

parts.note: to pot is to shoot game
a gap is an interval

explanation.surface: A replacement player shoots high just before half-time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skyward' turns POTS into STOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporary measure filling in until something better arrives is a makeshift.

clue.text: Thoroughly useless husband restricting daughter

indicators.note: restricting means the hopeless husband hems the daughter in

parts.note: inept means useless or incompetent

explanation.surface: A domestic complaint: an incompetent husband keeping a daughter on a tight rein.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricting' puts the daughter within the useless-husband pair, just after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with full detail and thoroughness is the same as covering it comprehensively.

clue.text: Republican in bad odour has a point

indicators.note: in means the Republican letter sits inside the smell

parts.note: a pong is a bad smell

explanation.surface: A politician caught in a scandal still makes a fair argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad odour' suggests disgrace, as in being in bad odour, but it is just a smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A tine of a fork is a sharp projecting spike.

clue.text: Start to finish, repeatedly enjoy success in pool where writers took a dip

indicators.note: start to finish means the opening letter goes to the end

parts.note: to sink and to pot both mean getting a ball in a pocket at pool, so two successes in a row

explanation.surface: A puzzling scene of swimming success in a pool where authors went bathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to finish' moves the S at the front of SINKPOT to the end. 'Pool' is the cue game, not a swimming bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers with dip pens dipped the nib into small ink containers on the desk, so that is where they dipped.

clue.text: Nasal passages endlessly employed

indicators.note: endlessly means both end letters are taken off

parts.note: sinuses are the cavities behind the nose

explanation.surface: Blocked noses working constantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' strips the first and last S from SINUSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Something currently being employed is occupied and being utilised.

clue.text: Body's a ton, approximately

parts.note: or so means approximately

explanation.surface: A heavy remark that someone's body weighs about a ton.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the human form, without head or limbs, is the main part of the physique.

clue.text: Throbbing ear — a lug in pain

indicators.note: throbbing suggests pulsing about, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A sore ear described as aching in pain. 'Lug' is slang for ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throbbing' rearranges EAR A LUG IN.
explanation.definitionFit: This is nerve pain, a sharp intermittent ache along the course of a nerve.

clue.text: Noise of train overheard by coastal resident

indicators.note: overheard means the word is listened to and spelt as a different word that sounds the same

parts.note: a steam engine's puffing noise is a chuff

explanation.surface: Someone living by the sea is bothered by the sound of passing trains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resident' suggests a person, but it is a bird. The chough is a red-billed crow of Cornish and Welsh sea cliffs.
explanation.definitionFit: This red-legged crow nests on rocky cliffs by the sea, so it lives on the coast.

clue.text: Spooner says to say "pardon" is a failing

indicators.note: Spooner, the Oxford don famed for swapping initial sounds, signals the swap

parts.note: to speak is to say something
pardon? and what? are both ways to ask someone to repeat

explanation.surface: Asking someone to repeat themselves is presented as a social shortcoming.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of 'speak what' gives 'weak spot'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vulnerable point or flaw in someone's character is a shortcoming.
